'''Riccardo D'Auria''' (born 1940) is an Italian [[theoretical physicist]] and an [[emeritus]] full professor of the [[Polytechnic University of Turin]].<ref name="Riccardopolito">{{Cite web |date=2022-10-14 |title=Riccardo D'Auria {{!}} Politecnico di Torino |url=https://www.polito.it/en/staff?p=riccardo.dauria |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=www.polito.it |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Riccardo D'Auria was born in [[Rome]], Italy in 1940. He graduated in Physics at the [[University of Turin]], under the supervision of Prof. [[Tullio Regge]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Le tesi dell'Università degli Studi di Torino |url=https://www.asut.unito.it/tesi/web/index.php?TesiSearch%5BCODICE_TESI%5D=&TesiSearch%5BCOGNOME%5D=&TesiSearch%5BNOME%5D=Riccardo&TesiSearch%5BTITOLO_TESI%5D=&TesiSearch%5BDESC_FACOLTA%5D=&TesiSearch%5BDATA%5D=&TesiSearch%5BDISCIPLINA%5D=&TesiSearch%5BCOGNOME_RELATORE%5D=Regge&TesiSearch%5BNOME_RELATORE%5D=&r=tesi |access-date=2 June 2025 |website=www.asut.unito.it}}</ref>

== Career ==
He was an associate professor at the [[University of Turin]], a full professor at  [[University of Padua]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature?sort=mostrecent&size=25&page=1&q=a%20d%27auria,r.%20and%20aff%20Padua%20U.&ui-citation-summary=true |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> and, eventually, at the [[Polytechnic University of Turin]]. There he founded a theoretical physics group, oriented towards [[particle physics]], [[Field theory (physics)|field theory]], [[gravity]] and [[supergravity]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DISAT - Theory of Fundamental Interactions |url=https://www.disat.polito.it/en/research/research_groups/fundint/theory_of_fundamental_interactions |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=DISAT |language=en-GB}}</ref> From 1996 to 2000 he was director of the Department of Physics of the [[Polytechnic University of Turin]].<ref name="Riccardopolito" />

He spent several extended periods at [[CERN]]<ref>[https://inspirehep.net/literature?sort=mostrecent&size=250&page=1&q=%20215854%20or%20218150%20or%20427660%20or%20513873&ui-citation-summary=true "R. D'Auria's papers with CERN affiliation"], INSPIRE HEP, Retrieved 2025-06-02</ref> and at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/450831 |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>

== Contributions ==
Riccardo D'Auria contributed, in the early years of [[superstring theory]] and in collaboration with a group of string theorists, to the introduction of internal [[Flavour (particle physics)|flavour symmetry]] and [[Color charge|color]] symmetry in a string algebra.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ademollo |first=M. |last2=Brink |first2=L. |last3=D'Adda |first3=A. |last4=D'Auria |first4=R. |last5=Napolitano |first5=E. |last6=Sciuto |first6=S. |last7=Del Giudice |first7=E. |last8=Di Vecchia |first8=P. |last9=Ferrara |first9=S. |last10=Gliozzi |first10=F. |last11=Musto |first11=R. |last12=Pettorino |first12=R. |last13=Schwarz |first13=J.H. |date=1976 |title=Dual string with U(1) colour symmetry |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321376904831 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=111 |issue=1 |pages=77–110 |bibcode=1976NuPhB.111...77A |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(76)90483-1|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Pietro G. Frè]] (and following a proposal by Y. Ne'eman and [[Tullio Regge|T. Regge]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ne'eman |first=Yuval |last2=Regge |first2=Tullio |date=1978 |title=Gravity and supergravity as gauge theories on a group manifold |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269378900588 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=74 |issue=1–2 |pages=54–56 |bibcode=1978PhLB...74...54N |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(78)90058-8|url-access=subscription }}</ref>), he developed a new approach to [[supergravity]] called ''[[nlab:D'Auria-Fré-Regge+formulation+of+supergravity|geometric or rheonomic approach]]''. Of special interest is the application of this approach to the study of theories where the physical fields include p-forms of degree higher than one, in particular, the [[eleven-dimensional supergravity]], the low-energy description of [[M-theory]].  By a generalisation of the [[Maurer-Cartan equation|Cartan-Maurer equations]] of an ordinary [[Graded Lie algebra|(graded) Lie algebra]], a new graded algebra was introduced, called [[nlab:D'Auria-Fré-Regge+formulation+of+supergravity|Cartan integrable system]], by means of which a geometric approach to higher-dimensional theories can be realised<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1982 |title=Geometric supergravity in D = 11 and iot hidden supergroup |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321382902814 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=206 |issue=3 |pages=496 |bibcode=1982NuPhB.206R.496. |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(82)90281-4|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
This mathematical structure is the first example of an  [[L-infinity algebra]] developed in mathematics some ten years after their original results, and formulated in the space dual to the space of differential p-forms.

In collaboration with [[Tullio Regge]], R. D'Auria explicitly constructed an [[Asymptotically flat spacetime|asymptotically flat]] [[gravitational instanton]] solution<ref>{{Cite journal |last=D'Auria |first=R. |last2=Regge |first2=T. |date=1982 |title=Gravity theories with asymptotically flat instantons |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321382904023 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=195 |issue=2 |pages=308–324 |bibcode=1982NuPhB.195..308D |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(82)90402-3|url-access=subscription }}</ref> of the four-dimensional [[The Einstein Theory of Relativity|Einstein theory]].

He also completed, with Leonardo Castellani and [[Sergio Ferrara]], the full formulation of [[Special Kähler geometry|Special Kaehler Geometry]], which allows the precise formulation of N=2 [[supergravity]] in four dimensions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castellani |first=L |last2=D'Auria |first2=R |last3=Ferrara |first3=S |date=1990-10-01 |title=Special geometry without special coordinates |url=http://cds.cern.ch/record/209229/files/cer-000121157.pdf |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=7 |issue=10 |pages=1767–1790 |bibcode=1990CQGra...7.1767C |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/7/10/009 |issn=0264-9381}}</ref> This eventually led him, within a different collaboration, to obtain the result of constructing the most general matter-coupled N=2 [[supergravity]] in four dimensions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Andrianopoli |first=L. |last2=Bertolini |first2=M. |last3=Ceresole |first3=A. |last4=D'Auria |first4=R. |last5=Ferrara |first5=S. |last6=Fré |first6=P. |last7=Magri |first7=T. |date=1997 |title=N = 2 supergravity and N = 2 super Yang-Mills theory on general scalar manifolds: Symplectic covariance gaugings and the momentum map |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0393044097000028 |journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics |language=en |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=111–189 |arxiv=hep-th/9605032 |bibcode=1997JGP....23..111A |doi=10.1016/S0393-0440(97)00002-8}}</ref>
